title: Near-real-time provider engagement notifications and consistent star rating display

requirements.text: Implement a near-real-time (“instant”) engagement-status notification experience between client and provider by refreshing provider engagement state automatically while the client is viewing that provider, and showing a clear in-app notification when the status changes between “Engaged” and “Not Engaged”.

quotes: let it be a live connection between the service provider and the client nofitying them if they are engaged or not engaged. it should be instantenous.

acceptanceCriteria: When a client is on the Provider Preview dialog or Provider Detail page for a specific provider, the UI automatically refreshes that provider’s engagement status without the user manually refreshing the page.

If the provider’s engagement status changes while the client is on the preview/detail UI, the client sees an in-app notification that clearly states the new status in English (e.g., “Provider is now Engaged” / “Provider is now Not Engaged”).
The refreshed engagement status is reflected in the visible status badge/text within 3 seconds of the provider saving a new engagement status (best-effort via polling).
The implementation does not use WebSockets or real-time chat transport; it uses safe periodic refresh (polling) of existing backend query data (e.g., provider preview / provider profile queries).

requirements.text: Ensure the backend engagement status update API is complete and reliably persists provider engagement status changes so clients can observe the updated value through existing read/query APIs.

quotes: let it be a live connection between the service provider and the client nofitying them if they are engaged or not engaged. it should be instantenous.

acceptanceCriteria: A signed-in Service Provider can update their engagement status, and the value persists in the provider profile (the existing `isEngaged` field).
Client-facing queries used by the UI (e.g., provider preview / provider read methods) return the updated `isEngaged` value after the provider updates it.
Unauthorized callers cannot update another provider’s engagement status.

requirements.text: Create and display a clear 1–5 star rating UI for service providers across client-facing provider surfaces, using English labels and consistent visuals (stars), including an explicit empty-state when a provider has no ratings yet.

quotes: also create a star rating for the service provider

acceptanceCriteria: Provider cards, provider preview, and provider detail views show a star-based rating display (not only a text/emoji-only rating) when ratings exist.
If a provider has no ratings yet, the UI shows an English empty state such as “No ratings yet” (or equivalent) instead of hiding the rating row entirely.
Any existing job-completion rating flow remains functional and continues to contribute to the provider’s average rating display.
All user-facing rating text is in English.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in `backend/main.mo` (no additional backend services).
Do not edit files in `frontend/src/components/ui` or other immutable frontend paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.
Do not use WebSockets/Socket.io/push notifications for “instant” updates; implement best-effort near-real-time behavior via polling/refresh of existing query APIs.
Keep the existing provider engagement field name and meaning (`isEngaged`: Bool) and expose it through existing provider read/preview APIs.
nonGoals: Implementing true real-time server push (WebSockets) or background notifications outside the currently open UI.
Adding third-party rating providers or external databases.
Changing the payment/unlock or messaging feature scope beyond what is needed to display engagement updates and ratings.
